growth_stages.notes: Photosynthesis and vegetative growth impacts documented mainly above ~38C.
sources: Crafts-Brandner & Salvucci 2002, cited in Djalovic et al., The Plant Genome (2024)

growth_stages.notes: Male flower organs (tassels) are the most heat-vulnerable tissue; anther dehiscence and pollen viability/germination are directly impaired.
growth_stages.reference_detail: Moderate heat stress (35/25C day/night for 48h) during the pollen tetrad stage greatly reduces kernel number per ear by impeding pollen viability.
sources: Djalovic et al., The Plant Genome (2024) - https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/tpg2.20378
Begcy et al. 2019, cited in Djalovic et al. 2024

growth_stages.notes: Silks (female reproductive tissue) are directly exposed to ambient heat; heat stress causes cell death in silk hairs and pollen-tube growth arrest, reducing seed set.
growth_stages.reference_detail: 35/25C day/night heat stress on silks 3 days after emergence caused silk-hair cell death rising from 1.5% (control) to 62-65% after 24-48h exposure.
sources: Heat-stress-induced ROS in maize silks..., iScience/ScienceDirect (2024) - https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2589004224013063

growth_stages.notes: Prolonged exposure above 35C during the reproductive stage is detrimental to reproductive success, seed set, and yield.
sources: Shao et al. 2021, cited in Djalovic et al., The Plant Genome (2024)

engine_notes: 35C is a recurring experimental threshold across multiple independent maize studies for the tasseling/silking window, giving it more confidence than a single-study figure. Field microclimate and genotype still shift the real threshold.
